findings.title: Membership response bit selects the opposite accumulator verifier
findings.source_claim: Query returns bit1 with inclusion and bit0 with non-inclusion; Verify dispatches oppositely
findings.check: For a sound complete accumulator and valid VRF proof, either honest membership response is sent to a verifier of a false proposition; rejects. Independent two-case abstraction agrees.
assumptions: Consistent addressing granted only to isolate dispatch
findings.counterevidence: A local specification repair is available; separate deployed/model-signing code is not shown to use this branch reversal. Neither fact rescues correctness of the published core protocol.
findings.impact: Dataset commitment and membership proofs are the second explicitly listed technical contribution; Section 6.3 uses the faulty verifier to realize it. Honest completeness of this contribution fails.

repair.statement: Reject nonbinary responses; dispatch bit1 to inclusion, bit0 to non-inclusion
repair.verification: Analytic and finite local dispatch check only

findings.title: Commitment and query use hashed versus raw VRF addresses
findings.source_claim: Commit uses H(VRF.Eval), while Query/Verify pass raw VRF.Eval to Acc
findings.check: Write raw output y. Commitment address H(y) is not definitionally equal to queried address y; no H(y)=y assumption is supplied.
findings.counterevidence: An implicit conversion could have been intended, but the raw output is required for VRF verification and its hashed index must be distinguished explicitly. No flaw in SEEMless, Parakeet or the primitives is asserted.
findings.impact: This is the same core dataset membership construction, and it remains inconsistent after F01 is corrected. A consistent address is necessary for its membership-proving operations.

repair.statement: Keep raw y for VRF verification and compute j=H(y) consistently for accumulator operations
repair.verification: Symbolic address invariant only; conditional on specified authenticated-map API

findings.title: Reported signing overhead interval differs from displayed total-minus-hash values
findings.check: Displayed differences span0.43-0.90s, whereas prose says0.478-0.602s; rounding cannot reconcile0.90.
findings.alternative: Prose may isolate a narrower stage; raw data needed
findings.impact: Bounded timing report; large-model hashing dominance unaffected
